title: NAS vs Mini PC for a Plex or Jellyfin Media Server
summary: Streaming subscriptions keep getting pricier. Should your home media server be a NAS or a mini PC? A head-to-head with the boxes and drives I'd use.
body_markdown:
A meme about streaming services raising prices and adding ads was one of the most upvoted posts on r/pcmasterrace last week, with over 28,000 upvotes. The comments were full of people tired of paying more to watch ads. If you'd rather own your media and stream it around your home, the first question is a simple one: should the server be a NAS or a mini PC?


Here is how the two approaches actually compare.


## The Contenders


**A NAS** is built around storage. Drive bays, RAID, snapshots and an operating system designed to run 24/7 come standard, and Plex or Jellyfin run as apps on top.


**A mini PC** is a small, quiet computer. It's more flexible, can run Windows or Linux, and its Intel chip handles video transcoding well, but storage is something you add, usually over USB or through internal M.2 slots.


Both options here use Intel processors with Quick Sync, which is what makes hardware transcoding work for 4K streams to phones and older TVs. One licensing note: Plex lists hardware-accelerated streaming as a Plex Pass feature, and since 2025 remote playback of personal video has required a Plex Pass or Remote Watch Pass. Jellyfin is free and supports hardware transcoding without a subscription.

## Deep Dive


### UGREEN NASync DXP2800


The[UGREEN NASync DXP2800](https://www.newegg.com/p/N82E16822995001?utm_source=insider&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=insider_article_nas-vs-mini-pc-plex-jellyfin-media-server) is the NAS I'd suggest to most first-timers. It has an Intel N100, 8GB of DDR5, two SATA bays for hard drives, two M.2 slots for SSD storage, and a 2.5GbE port. Two drives in RAID 1 give you one drive's worth of protected space, which is enough for a starting library.


### UGREEN NASync DXP4800 Plus


Once a library outgrows two drives, the[UGREEN NASync DXP4800 Plus](https://www.newegg.com/p/N82E16822995003?utm_source=insider&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=insider_article_nas-vs-mini-pc-plex-jellyfin-media-server) is where I'd go. It has four bays, a 5-core Pentium Gold 8505, 8GB of DDR5 expandable to 64GB, RAID 5, 6 and 10 support, and both 10GbE and 2.5GbE ports. The 10GbE port is overkill for streaming but very useful when copying a whole Blu-ray collection onto it.


### Synology DS225+


The[Synology DS225+](https://www.newegg.com/p/N82E16822108853?utm_source=insider&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=insider_article_nas-vs-mini-pc-plex-jellyfin-media-server) is the choice if you value Synology's DSM software and its backup and photo apps. Its Celeron J4125 is older than UGREEN's chips, and memory tops out at 6GB. Synology's drive policy for its 2025 Plus models caused a stir, but DSM 7.3, released in October 2025, restored support for third-party hard drives such as Seagate and WD on models like this one.


### Beelink Mini S13


The[Beelink Mini S13](https://www.newegg.com/p/9SIBSMJKPK0260?utm_source=insider&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=insider_article_nas-vs-mini-pc-plex-jellyfin-media-server) is the minimal option. It has an Intel N150 with 4 cores up to 3.6GHz, 12GB of non-expandable LPDDR5, a 512GB SSD with room to add M.2 storage, 2.5GbE and Windows 11 Home. Paired with an external drive such as the[WD Elements 16TB desktop drive](https://www.newegg.com/p/N82E16822234435?utm_source=insider&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=insider_article_nas-vs-mini-pc-plex-jellyfin-media-server) , it's one of the quickest ways to get a Plex or Jellyfin server running in an afternoon. The trade-off: there's no redundancy unless you add a second drive and back it up yourself.


### Beelink ME Pro


The[Beelink ME Pro](https://www.newegg.com/p/9SIBSMJKTR6351?utm_source=insider&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=insider_article_nas-vs-mini-pc-plex-jellyfin-media-server) sits between the two categories. It's a mini PC with the same N150, 16GB of LPDDR5 and a 1TB SSD, but it adds two drive bays for 2.5-inch or 3.5-inch SATA drives and three M.2 2280 slots. Beelink pitches it for Jellyfin, Plex or Kodi, and its drawer-style design is meant for easy upgrades later.


### The Drives


For drives that spin all day, I'd use NAS models rather than desktop drives. The[Seagate IronWolf 8TB](https://www.newegg.com/p/N82E16822184796?utm_source=insider&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=insider_article_nas-vs-mini-pc-plex-jellyfin-media-server) is a 7,200RPM CMR drive with 256MB of cache. The[WD Red Plus 8TB](https://www.newegg.com/p/1Z4-0002-01NP7?utm_source=insider&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=insider_article_nas-vs-mini-pc-plex-jellyfin-media-server) spins slower at 5,640RPM, which usually means less noise, is rated for up to 180TB per year of workload and carries a 3-year limited warranty. Either works well in these boxes. I'd lean toward the WD in a living room, where noise matters more.


## Winner by Category


- **Best for most people:** UGREEN NASync DXP2800 with two 8TB NAS drives.
- **Best for a growing library:** UGREEN NASync DXP4800 Plus.
- **Best software ecosystem:** Synology DS225+.
- **Fastest setup:** Beelink Mini S13 plus a WD Elements external drive.
- **Best hybrid:** Beelink ME Pro.


If your media matters to you, I'd pick a NAS for the redundancy alone. If you just want to try self-hosting and see if you like it, a mini PC is cheap and quiet and won't lock you in. Newegg has more options under[NAS listings](https://www.newegg.com/p/pl?d=nas&utm_source=insider&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=insider_article_nas-vs-mini-pc-plex-jellyfin-media-server) .


## Frequently Asked Questions


**Is a NAS or a mini PC better for Plex?** A NAS is better if you want drive redundancy and 24/7 storage features. A mini PC is cheaper to start and more flexible, but you need to add and back up storage yourself.


**Does Plex need a Plex Pass for hardware transcoding?** Yes. Plex lists hardware-accelerated streaming as a Plex Pass feature. Jellyfin supports hardware transcoding for free.


**Do I need a Plex Pass to stream my media outside my home?** Plex says remote playback of personal video requires an active Plex Pass on the server admin or your account, or a Remote Watch Pass.


**Can the Synology DS225+ use Seagate or WD hard drives?** Yes. DSM 7.3, released in October 2025, restored support for third-party HDDs and SATA SSDs on 2025 Plus models such as the DS225+.


**Which processor is good for a Jellyfin or Plex server?** Intel chips with Quick Sync, such as the N100, N150 and Pentium Gold 8505, handle hardware transcoding efficiently in small, low-power boxes.
